way.d: how something is done or how it happens

ways and means.d: resources available to meet expenses (especially legislation for raising revenue for a government)

way station.d: a small railway station between the principal stations or a station where the train stops only on a signal

way out.d: an opening that permits escape or release

wayne.d: American general during the American Revolution (1745-1796)

wayfaring tree.d: vigorous deciduous European treelike shrub common along waysides; red berries turn black

wayside.d: edge of a way or road or path

wayfarer.d: a traveler going on a trip

wayland.d: a supernatural smith and king of the elves; identified with Norse Volund

waybill.d: a receipt given by the carrier to the shipper acknowledging receipt of the goods being shipped and specifying the terms of delivery
